title: Private Deploy: Minimal External Surface & Canary Probe Acceptance Criteria
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: define a compact, testable set of requirements and acceptance gates for Private/VPC deployments that minimize external network surface area while preserving safe upgrades. This ticket clarifies scope (networking limits, upgrade canaries, air-gapped install modes), documents concrete probe definitions, and enumerates operator runbook checks required for release approval.

Scope clarifications (in/out):
- IN: Network allowlist contract for bootstrap & artifact retrieval, deterministic canary probes to validate operator/agent health, upgrade gating criteria for staged rollouts in air-gapped and low-egress environments, checksum/image-signing validation, and required telemetry for post-upgrade verification.
- OUT: Changes to public hosted API pricing, Dedicated autoscaling policies, or new hardware procurement. Those will be separate tickets.

Background/why: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs frequently restrict egress to a narrow set of endpoints. Upgrades must be safe when mirrors or offline artifact distribution are used. Current ambiguity in what probes constitute a successful canary causes inconsistent rollouts and occasional emergency rollbacks. We need a minimal, reproducible acceptance checklist that engineering and support can use to validate private deployments during onboarding and upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Network contract: default cluster configuration must operate with only four allowed outbound targets (image mirror, checksum/manifest verification endpoint, KMS unwrap endpoint or local KMS proxy, and metrics ingestion endpoint) unless the customer explicitly approves additional targets.

No hidden egress: operator binary and runtime may not open outbound connections to additional IPs outside the allowlist during bootstrap or upgrades in the default configuration. Automated tests must prove this in CI using a simulated deny-all egress firewall.

Canary probes defined: three independent probe types must run post-deploy: (1) bootstrap artifact probe — attempts to fetch current release from configured mirror and validates image signature checksum; (2) operator-heartbeat probe — internal HTTP probe that verifies agent registration and KV-sync latency; (3) workload-inference smoke probe — runs a short, deterministic model inference (<=64 tokens) against the deployed runtime and validates latency and output structure. All probes must include detailed log output for debugging.

Probe success thresholds: 99% artifact fetch success within 180s across 3 consecutive runs; operator-heartbeat latency p50 < 200ms and p95 < 500ms; smoke-inference latency p50 < 120ms and deterministic output schema match for 100% of runs.

Upgrade gating: rollout must halt and auto-rollback if any canary type fails 3 times within a 10-minute window during a canary cohort. Rollout controller must surface clear error codes and a one-click rollback path for operators.

Air-gapped acceptance: offline bootstrap path (mirror or physical media) must include a reproducible checksum reconciliation step and an operator-local signature verification flow. The ticket must include a documented manual verification sequence for customers and an automated test harness that can be run in the CI mirror environment.

Image provenance: every release artifact used in Private must be signed and accompanied by a signed manifest; operator will reject unsigned or checksum-mismatched images when 'strict_image_provenance' flag is enabled (default for regulated customers).

Observability: private deployment console must show per-cohort canary metrics for the last 24 hours and provide a linkable trace for each failed canary event. Dashboards used in acceptance must be reachable in the tenant console or via a shared read-only Grafana URL.

Documentation & runbooks: an operator runbook for Canary failure modes must be authored, containing triage steps, required logs, and recommended mitigations (mirror cutover, certificate renewal, KMS rewrap). The runbook must be reviewed and approved by SRE and Security.

Test coverage: end-to-end integration tests that simulate restricted egress and offline-mirror bootstraps must exist in the private-operator repo and run in CI nightly. Tests must be annotated with the ticket URL and pass consistently before release sign-off.
test_plan: Add a CI job that spawns a test VPC with deny-by-default egress rules and runs the three canary probes against a configured local mirror; job must fail if any egress outside the allowlist is detected.

Create a lab procedure for manual air-gapped bootstrap: publish a step-by-step checklist for imaging a mirror, copying artifacts via physical media, and running checksum reconciliation on the target cluster.
Simulate upgrade rollouts with injected failure modes (mirror latency, signature mismatch, KMS unwrap failure) and verify rollout halts and rollback executes with observability events captured.
Run smoke-inference probe against an ensemble of model sizes and ensure deterministic schema validation and latency assertions hold across quantized and full-precision variants.
operational_notes: If a customer requires additional outbound endpoints, require a signed change request and update the cluster allowlist managed artifact. Keep extra endpoints scoped to CIDRs and documented in the tenant contract.
For KMS in air-gapped mode, prefer local HSM or a pre-wrapped key artifact delivered via mirror; documented operator flow must support a manual key import path.
During canary failures, automatically collect operator logs, recent artifact manifests, and the last 5 probe traces and attach them to the incident ticket for faster TTR.
